> When we use the term "union", do we mean:
> 
> • any authorizer may allow the request • all authorizers must allow the request • there might be multiple authorizers and we are unsure how they might be related

I asked because different interpretations might lead to people implementing something accidentally vulnerable, and we should try too avoid that.

> When we use the term "union", do we mean:
> • any authorizer may allow the request
> • all authorizers must allow the request
> • there might be multiple authorizers and we are unsure how they might be related

@lmktfy Thanks for the question. It's the same as the union authorizer of Kubernetes, namely that authorizers are priority-ordered, and the highest-priority one that returns `Allow` or `Deny` gets its way. Let's see if we can make that clearer in the comments somewhere. However, users are not meant to use the union `ConditionsAwareDecision` directly, but just indirectly through using the union authorizer. Alternatively, we could try to be extra defensive and try to make it impossible for anyone except the union authorizer to use it 🤔

@neolit123 Thanks for the alternative approach. I see a couple issues with flattening the tree:
- (I think) it means that the `AuthorizerName` needs to be unique in the whole tree, instead of like now, unique per union authorizer. 
- I'd like to keep the information if possible from `NoOpinion` decision in the middle of the union, as it might give us information about an error that occurred, this controls whether the response is 500 or 403, if no `Allow` decisions were found
- Performing `EvaluateCondition` on a single leaf `ConditionsMap` might not necessarily be possible in the presence of webhook authorizers, given a tree of form
  - union A
    - foo
    - webhook
      - union B
        - bar
        - baz

the outermost union authorizer would first try to evaluate `foo` in-process by calling `foo.EvaluateConditions`, but it cannot call `bar/baz.EvaluateConditions` as those authorizers exist in another process. What happens instead is that the webhook authorizer sends the whole sub-tree of union B through the webhook to the process that authored it.

Does this rationale make sense to you?

> * (I think) it means that the AuthorizerName needs to be unique in the whole tree, instead of like now, unique per union authorizer.

yep, the per process name uniqueness is already required as far as can tell:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/586cc904093af4fe7492e564908a796f0b107f97/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/apis/apiserver/validation/validation.go#L632

> *I'd like to keep the information if possible from NoOpinion decision in the middle of the union, as it might give us information about an error that occurred, this controls whether the response is 500 or 403, if no Allow decisions were found

that's a problem with the alternative, yes. 
could be fixed if ConditionsAwareAuthorize(), keeps tracks of not only the conditionsMaps but also of the noOpinion{Errors|Reasons}, then returns different errors.

> * Performing `EvaluateCondition` on a single leaf `ConditionsMap` might not necessarily be possible in the presence of webhook authorizers, given a tree of form
>   
>   * union A
>     
>     * foo
>     * webhook
>       
>       * union B
>         
>         * bar
>         * baz
> 
> the outermost union authorizer would first try to evaluate `foo` in-process by calling `foo.EvaluateConditions`, but it cannot call `bar/baz.EvaluateConditions` as those authorizers exist in another process. What happens instead is that the webhook authorizer sends the whole sub-tree of union B through the webhook to the process that authored it.

cross process boundary would be a problem if it has to call bar.EvaluateConditaions directly from union A.
is that a requirement? i would have assumed that union A only calls webhook and it never knows about its internals. a decision from webhook doesn't leak the children structure either.

reviews.body:
@luxas if you are interested, i vibe-coded an alternative approach that IMHO simplifies the design by adding ownership to a conditions map and removes things like  `conditionsAwareDecisionTypeUnion`  and `conditionsAwareDecisionUnionSlice` (which confused me the most), but still allows cross process handling, and all use cases, IIUC. 

since i am not an expert in this area, please ignore if this is junk...

an authorizerName is now part of CondtionsMap, defining clear ownership.

```
type ConditionsMap struct {
	authorizerName      string
	denyConditions      []Condition
	noOpinionConditions []Condition
	allowConditions     []Condition
}
```

the decision has no union any more and can return a slice of condition maps:

```
func (d ConditionsAwareDecision) IsAllow() bool
func (d ConditionsAwareDecision) IsDeny() bool
func (d ConditionsAwareDecision) IsNoOpinion() bool
func (d ConditionsAwareDecision) IsUnconditional() bool
func (d ConditionsAwareDecision) IsConditional() bool
func (d ConditionsAwareDecision) UnconditionalParts() (Decision, string, error)
func (d ConditionsAwareDecision) ConditionsMaps() []ConditionsMap
func (d ConditionsAwareDecision) Reason() string
func (d ConditionsAwareDecision) Error() error
func (d ConditionsAwareDecision) String() string
```

> Add an authorizerName string field to ConditionsMap. This is the name by which the owning authorizer is registered in the chain. With this field present, the
union authorizer can route a ConditionsMap back to its owner by name lookup
rather than by index position.
> 
> Replace the Union decision type with a flat []ConditionsMap slice on
ConditionsAwareDecision, collected by the union authorizer as it walks the
chain. A fallback field holds the first unconditional Allow or Deny seen after
the conditions, or NoOpinion if the chain was exhausted.
> 
> ConditionsAwareDecision then has three variants instead of five:
Allow, Deny, and NoOpinion. The conditional case is represented by a non-empty
conditionsMaps slice on any of these, with IsConditional() returning true when
that slice is non-empty.
